questions.prompt: An analyst proposes a seven-level firmware scale: the first level is always caught and the last can only be identified using TPM. Assess what evidence this scale supplies.
A lab log records an EPT write exit while a PCIe device is attached. What can be attributed to that device and what additional boundary matters?
A freshly verified TPM quote matches the selected PCR reference values. What can be concluded about all runtime game behavior?
A render log records 100 Present calls. What evidence is needed to claim 100 monitor-displayed frames?
A pixel shader returns red with alpha 0.5. A report says this proves depth testing was bypassed. Assess the report from pipeline evidence.
A binary comparison tool yields a similarity score and an instrumentation run observes all input-exercised edges. Assess whether this establishes best tool quality or complete program behavior.

results.answer: The seven levels are an unsupported classification, not measured detection evidence. Neither guaranteed detection at the first level nor TPM-only identification at the last follows from a firmware label. Evaluate identity/provenance, configuration/function, runtime behavior, active remapping policy and platform trust separately, with exact versions, collection coverage, matched benign baselines and measured decision error rates; TPM is neither established as necessary nor sufficient.

The log establishes a processor-side write access that violated the active EPT policy, assuming a trustworthy collector and correct interpretation. Device attachment alone does not attribute that access, a DMA transaction, or malicious intent to the PCIe device. Device-to-memory access crosses the separate IOMMU/VT-d boundary: establish the requester, active domain/mappings, topology and collector coverage, and corroborate with device-request/fault or other platform evidence. Hypervisor presence does not prove either path is covered.

No conclusion about all runtime game behavior follows. A fresh, verified quote matching the reference supports acceptance of the selected PCR measurements under the enrollment, verifier trust and appraisal policy; their meaning also depends on the bank, platform profile and trustworthy measurement/event-log relationship. It does not certify unmeasured runtime actions, enumerate current devices or authenticate every current IOMMU mapping. Those claims need separate runtime evidence.

One hundred Present calls establish one hundred observed API invocations, not one hundred monitor-displayed frames. Preserve call results/flags, swap-chain identity, presentation model, OS/driver/compositor configuration, target output and timestamps, then correlate the submissions with trustworthy display-stage evidence showing which actually reached that monitor, accounting for discarded submissions, repeats and missing observations. Define whether the count means distinct submissions, complete images or display refreshes. Render-target readback, compositor capture and PresentMon metrics each have their own coverage limits; none is automatically a physical-display image observation.

The report is unsupported: red output with alpha 0.5 is shader-output evidence, not proof that depth testing was bypassed. Actual visibility depends on output-merger blending and depth/stencil processing. Inspect the shader identity, bound pipeline/depth-stencil and blending state, render/depth targets, draw order and captured event context, then compare with the expected material/pass and legitimate visualization modes. Color or alpha alone establishes neither a depth-state change nor malicious intent.

Neither claim is established. A similarity score is candidate matching evidence; a best-tool ranking requires a specified comparative benchmark and independently checked matches, preserving tool versions, input hashes, architecture, compiler/optimization changes and unmatched functions. The trace supports only observed edges for the stated inputs, threads and intervals. Record the coverage unit/denominator, missing code or events, semantic fidelity and instrumentation effects; exercised-edge coverage does not establish every feasible path, path combination, state or complete program behavior. Corroborate semantic-change claims before assigning security impact.

qualified_technical_review.root_assessment: All six answers preserve the relevant evidence boundary; no material error was identified in this bounded review. This is a qualitative review, not a population accuracy estimate.
